title: Multivariate Gaussian Integral via Matrix Diagonalization

problemStatement.formal: theorem multivariate_gaussian_integral (n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hA : A.PosDef) : ∫ x : Fin n → ℝ, Real.exp (-(Matrix.dotProduct x (A.mulVec x))) = Real.sqrt (Real.pi ^ n / A.det)
problemStatement.plain: For a positive-definite real symmetric matrix A of size n×n, prove ∫_{ℝⁿ} exp(-xᵀAx) dx = √(πⁿ/det(A)) by diagonalizing A via the spectral theorem.
whyMatters: Natural generalization of the scalar Gaussian integral in AreaOfCircleOQ05.lean
Used in multivariate normal distributions, statistics, and quantum mechanics
Requires spectral theorem + Fubini + measure theory — demonstrates Mathlib coverage

open: Spectral theorem change of variables for orthogonal Q

knowledge.progressSummary: Problem selected by Seeker. Parent has scalar Gaussian. Key approach: diagonalize A = Q^T D Q, use Fubini and scalar case per eigenvalue.
insights: Spectral theorem: symmetric positive-definite A = Q^T D Q, Q orthogonal
Change of variables y = Qx has Jacobian 1 (orthogonal Q)
Product of √(π/λᵢ) = √(πⁿ/det A) via det A = ∏ λᵢ
